question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $10x$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 5\cdot x,$ and the $12(x+1)$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10x}{12(x+1)}=\frac{2\cdot 5\cdot x}{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $2$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 5\cdot x}{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 5\cdot x}{\cancel{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{5\cdot x}{2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{5x}{6(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{5x}{6(x+1)}.$
